request.spec:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people list now has a sort select with the options added, name, grade and due-total. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The whole change is in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. Nothing is stored and the server is unchanged.

- **The select:** it sits above the people list (`data-testid="sort-by"`). Each signed-in user's choice is kept separately on that screen and starts at "added". If another user picks a sort on the same sheet, it doesn't change yours. Re-loading the sheet keeps your choice.
- **Name:** names are trimmed and compared ignoring case, the same way the app matches the signed-in user to a person.
- **Grade:** sorts A, B, C by each person's grade as of the sheet's today.
- **Due-total:** sorts on the value shown, after the cap, so changing the cap or adding a hold can change the order. People with no due-total (n/a) go last.
- **Ties:** people with the same key stay in list order.
- **What it doesn't touch:** only the order of the rows on screen changes. Positions, moving a person up or down, the rollup lines, the bulk "Move selected claims to" dropdown, exports and audit records all still follow the stored list order.
